Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 2f3ec36c6a7e7e6d4d78c7430f3d17ee8f71a464 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ejurgensen <espenjurgensen@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2019 19:15:31 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] [input] Fix for playback pause on http streams

This fixes a bug from commit 37ce8dd6 where seek_http (which is called when
pausing playback) for non-seekable streams would return -1, thus signalling
an error, even though it is not. The player would think that the stream
could not be played and then skip to the next item.

diff --git a/src/inputs/file_http.c b/src/inputs/file_http.c
index ca570ecb..9d6d8a38 100644
--- a/src/inputs/file_http.c
+++ b/src/inputs/file_http.c
@@ -123,9 +123,12 @@ seek(struct input_source *source, int seek_ms)
 static int
 seek_http(struct input_source *source, int seek_ms)
 {
-  // stream is live/unknown length so obvs can't seek
+  // Stream is live/unknown length so can't seek. We return 0 anyway, because
+  // it is valid for the input to request a seek, since the input is not
+  // supposed to concern itself about this.
   if (source->len_ms == 0)
-    return -1;
+    return 0;
+
   return transcode_seek(source->input_ctx, seek_ms);
 }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File Modified: `src/inputs/file_http.c`**
- The `seek_http` function was modified to change the return value when the stream length is unknown (i.e., `source->len_ms == 0`).
- The original return value of `-1` (indicating an error) was changed to `0`, which indicates that it is valid for the input to request a seek even if the stream cannot actually be sought.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification in `seek_http` addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (37ce8dd6) that incorrectly signaled an error for non-seekable streams. By returning `0` instead of `-1`, the patch ensures that the player does not mistakenly conclude that the stream cannot be played, thus preventing it from skipping to the next item unnecessarily. This change improves the handling of playback for HTTP streams, particularly those that are live or of unknown length.

Here is the commit message:
[input] Fix for playback pause on http streams

This fixes a bug from commit 37ce8dd6 where seek_http (which is called when
pausing playback) for non-seekable streams would return -1, thus signalling
an error, even though it is not. The player would think that the stream
could not be played and then skip to the next item.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `seek_http` function returning `-1` for non-seekable streams (where `source->len_ms == 0`), which incorrectly signaled an error to the player. This led the player to assume that the stream could not be played and prompted it to skip to the next item, even though it was valid for the input to request a seek in such cases.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int
 seek_http(struct input_source *source, int seek_ms)
 {
-  // stream is live/unknown length so obvs can't seek
+  // Stream is live/unknown length so can't seek. We return 0 anyway, because
+  // it is valid for the input to request a seek, since the input is not
+  // supposed to concern itself about this.
   if (source->len_ms == 0)
-    return -1;
+    return 0;
+
   return transcode_seek(source->input_ctx, seek_ms);
 }

```c
    return -1;
```
Reason:
The `seek_http` function checks if the stream length is unknown (i.e., `source->len_ms == 0`). In this case, it incorrectly returns `-1`, signaling an error to the player. This miscommunication leads the player to assume that the stream cannot be played, causing it to skip to the next item.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (source->len_ms == 0)
    return 0;
```
Reason:
The patch modifies the return value for non-seekable streams from `-1` to `0`. This change indicates that while seeking is not possible, it is not an error condition. This allows the player to understand that the stream is still valid and prevents it from skipping to the next item unnecessarily.
